summary.text: Gary Wilken is the Democratic candidate for the Wyoming House of Representatives, District 46, in the November 3, 2026 general election.
He advanced from the Democratic primary on August 18, 2026.
Wilken is a United Methodist pastor and police chaplain who worked for the Albany County Sheriff's Office.

paragraphs.text: Gary Wilken earned a high school diploma from Loveland High School, a bachelor's degree from Colorado State University in 1973, and a master's degree in divinity from the Pacific School of Religion in 1977.
He graduated from the Wyoming Law Enforcement Academy in 2003.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Wilken said he has lived in Laramie and worked for the Albany County Sheriff's Office since April 14, 1997, serving as a supervisor in the Detention Division, an instructor and field training officer, a liaison with the Drug Court program, and a chaplain.
He said that after a disability retirement in 2011 he was a code enforcement officer for the county planning office for nine years, and that he also served part time as a minister at two churches.

Wilken said Wyoming needs to partner to keep public lands open to the public, prioritize quality public education, make health care affordable, create living-wage jobs, and preserve family ranching and the rural lifestyle.
He named addiction, homelessness, domestic violence and a lack of well-paying jobs as challenges in Albany County.
